dependencyKindNote: RESOLVED under OWNER_CORRECTIONS_REQUIRED.json Q7, decided 2026-09-02. What was blocked was the prior question of whether a statewide form exists at all, together with the county MC case-type convention. The first is now answered from held sources: NO statewide form exists for an I.C. 34-28-5-15 infraction petition. Every Indiana PDF in the mounted Master Library (the Coalition for Court Access Section 1 non-conviction petition-and-order bundle, its inserts, its instructions, and the Section 2, 3 and 4 conviction inserts) and every Indiana PDF in the partial Nationwide custody was text-extracted on 2026-09-02 and none contains '34-28-5-15' or 'infraction'; every Coalition for Court Access instrument held is an I.C. 35-38-9 expungement form, a different chapter and a different remedy. The registry still records officialFormId null and officialSourceUrl null for this component, which is consistent with that answer rather than with an unsearched question. The second — the county MC case-type convention — is not a drafting question and never was: it is a caption blank, declared required before filing, with the clerk of the county named as the authority, which is what this family's own records already direct (manifest serve_party: 'Confirm local practice on the MC case-type assignment'; memo self-help stop condition: 'The county's MC case-type handling is unclear.').
conditionDescription: Stage 2, generated only where the court did not act, or after a deferral or satisfied judgment, once the form and MC case-type gates close.
blockingStatement: Resolved for drafting purposes. Whether a statewide form exists for an I.C. 34-28-5-15 infraction petition is answered: none exists in any source this repository holds, and outbound fetching of the Coalition for Court Access forms index was refused at CONNECT on 2026-09-02, so the answer rests on held sources. How Indiana counties handle the MC case-type assignment where no cause number was assigned remains unanswerable from any source and is carried to the participant as a caption blank with the clerk named.
exactMissingSource: Still outstanding as a source-lane acquisition, and no longer a drafting bar: live confirmation from the Coalition for Court Access expungement forms index at https://www.in.gov/courts/iocs/self-service/expungement/ that no statewide I.C. 34-28-5-15 infraction petition form has been published since 2026-07-30. The request was refused at CONNECT (HTTP 403) in the correction container on 2026-09-02 and the exact URL is recorded here rather than treated as absent. If such a form is later acquired, it governs and this composed petition becomes a support document or is withdrawn.

recordedButNotRendered.note: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-02: every item below is now rendered into the drafted petition, which is what this block was preserved for. It is kept verbatim so the drafted petition can be checked clause by clause against the registry statement it was drafted from.
recordedButNotRendered.venue: The court where the charges were brought or the trial was held, or the court with jurisdiction over the violation for a deferral participant. Filed under the original cause number, or as an MC case type if no cause number was assigned.
recordedButNotRendered.feeWaiver: Not applicable. There is no fee.
recordedButNotRendered.participantSignature: The petition is verified and signed by the petitioner.
recordedButNotRendered.service: Service on the prosecuting attorney. Confirm local practice on the MC case-type assignment.
recordedButNotRendered.notice: Service on the prosecuting attorney, who has thirty days to file a notice in opposition. The court may summarily grant, set a hearing, or summarily deny. A hearing is required if opposition is filed and the court does not rule summarily.
recordedButNotRendered.manualCompletionItem: Verification and signature - Petition, verification block. The participant signs it themselves once stage 2 becomes available.
